title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-08
ranking_basis: Daily GitHub Trending star gains for the nine captured trending repositories; verified repositories created/pushed in the last two days appended with unavailable daily gains.
ranking_explanation: Ranks 1–9 are ordered by GitHub Trending “stars today” as observed on 2026-11-08: Sherlock, OpenMausBot, Astryx, agent-browser, Anthropic Skills, billion-context, NVKE, Claude Quickstarts, then MuJoCo. Ranks 10–12 are supplemental recent repositories (Pinky, devvm, phoneuse), not ranked by daily star gain.
global_caveat: Trending gains and total stars are live counts that may change after capture. Supplemental recent repositories were selected from GitHub Search and checked against first-party READMEs; their daily star gains are not available from the matching Trending view. Several projects explicitly identify beta, preview, or experimental maturity.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Sherlock topped today’s gain signal (+2,372 stars), but agent workflows formed the broadest technology cluster: skills, browser control, desktop bots, context management, and fresh phone/sandbox projects. Recent additions Pinky and phoneuse point toward agents operating through user-visible devices, with human approval and maturity caveats that matter.

sections.title: sherlock-project/sherlock
sections.description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across 400+ social networks.
sections.why_notable: It leads today’s Trending snapshot by a wide margin, while remaining a practical OSINT utility rather than an AI project.
sections.content: Hunt down social media accounts by username across 400+ social networks. The README documents CLI searches and multiple output formats.

sections.title: milind-soni/OpenMausBot
sections.description: An open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine bots can use.
sections.why_notable: A strong second-place gain signal for the emerging “agents as chat contacts” desktop pattern.
sections.unique_caveat: Its README describes it as an independent project and says it is not affiliated with xAI, Meta, OpenAI, or Manus.
sections.content: A desktop chat interface for multiple AI bots, with individual agents, models, connected apps, and computer access; the README describes a local-first Claude/Codex-backed setup.

sections.title: meta/astryx
sections.description: An open-source design system that is customizable and agent-ready.
sections.why_notable: The strongest design-system signal in today’s list, joining component libraries with agent-assisted workflows.
sections.unique_caveat: The project README labels Astryx as currently in beta.
sections.content: A React 19 and StyleX design system with 150+ accessible components, theming, templates, and a CLI; its README says the system is in beta.

sections.title: vercel-labs/agent-browser
sections.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents.
sections.why_notable: It packages browser control as a compact shell-driven workflow and is among the day’s top agent-tooling gainers.
sections.content: A native Rust CLI exposes browser pages as compact accessibility snapshots with element references; agents act through short shell commands and re-check the result.

sections.title: anthropics/skills
sections.description: Anthropic’s public repository for Agent Skills.
sections.why_notable: Its high daily gain reflects continuing interest in reusable, task-specific agent capabilities and workflow packaging.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says this is Anthropic’s implementation of skills for Claude, not the Agent Skills standard itself.
sections.content: A set of self-contained skill folders combining instructions, scripts, and resources for specialized repeatable tasks; the repository includes examples across creative, technical, and enterprise workflows.

sections.title: ranxianglei/billion-context
sections.description: A context-compression plugin for long agent sessions and smaller context windows.
sections.why_notable: A distinct infrastructure angle on agent growth: keep long-running coding sessions within bounded model context.
sections.unique_caveat: Compression and benchmark figures in the README are project-reported claims, not independently validated in this snapshot.
sections.content: A proxy-style context manager that exposes compress, decompress, search, and status tools so the model can manage older conversation ranges.

sections.title: dsx-ai-factory/nvke
sections.description: A management plane for GPU Kubernetes on bare metal.
sections.why_notable: The clearest GPU-infrastructure entry: it manages independent Kubernetes workload clusters on NVIDIA hardware.
sections.unique_caveat: The README labels NVKE a preview and explicitly says it is not recommended for production workloads yet.
sections.content: A management plane provisions and lifecycle-manages isolated Kubernetes workload clusters through NVIDIA infrastructure; the README describes a preview-stage project.

sections.title: anthropics/claude-quickstarts
sections.description: Deployable application examples for developers building with the Claude API.
sections.why_notable: A low-gain counterpoint to fast-rising agent frameworks: first-party starter applications emphasize concrete deployment patterns.
sections.unique_caveat: These are example projects and require a Claude API key; they are not a general-purpose agent platform.
sections.content: The repository includes customer-support and financial-analysis examples, plus computer-use demos and best-practice guidance.

sections.title: google-deepmind/mujoco
sections.description: A general-purpose physics simulator for articulated structures and contact dynamics.
sections.why_notable: A useful non-agent counterpoint: today’s list still includes established simulation infrastructure for robotics and embodied research.
sections.content: A performance-oriented physics engine with a C API, native and browser visualization, Python bindings, and robotics/biomechanics use cases.

sections.title: DIYgod/pinky
sections.description: Let AI agents use your phone, with you in the loop.
sections.why_notable: A newly active project (created Nov 6, pushed Nov 8) that extends agent workflows from browsers and desktops to real phones.
sections.content: A cross-platform MCP gateway lets agents operate iPhone or Android devices while a person watches and approves risky actions; the README says approvals are enforced by Pinky’s gateway.

sections.title: devvmhq/devvm
sections.description: One isolated VM per project, ready for a developer or coding agent.
sections.why_notable: A fresh sandboxing workflow relevant to coding agents: project-specific VMs provide an isolated toolchain and workspace.
sections.content: A CLI creates isolated project VMs using Lima; the first-party README documents setup, safety guidance, and a project-folder quick start.

sections.title: lxe/phoneuse
sections.description: Operate an unmodified iPhone from Linux via screen mirroring and Bluetooth input.
sections.why_notable: A fresh, technically distinct device-control counterpoint: it combines AirPlay mirroring with Bluetooth HID and offers CLI/MCP access.
sections.unique_caveat: The README calls it a technology demo under heavy construction, tested on one specific iPhone/Linux/GPU setup.
sections.content: Lets a Linux PC mirror and control an unmodified iPhone, with optional agent access through a CLI or MCP; the project warns of narrow testing and ongoing construction.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The strongest single surge is a mature OSINT utility, while much of the remaining momentum is in making agents usable and governable through tools, interfaces, and persistent context. The newer phone and VM projects are early signals rather than proven platforms; NVKE is also explicitly preview-stage. Language counts across the 12 listed repos are Python 3, Go 3, TypeScript 3, Rust 1, C++ 1, and C 1.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary data: GitHub Trending today (https://github.com/trending?since=daily), observed at 2026-11-08 17:45 UTC. GitHub REST repository metadata and default-branch commits corroborated the nine Trending entries; `git ls-remote ... HEAD` resolved current default-branch HEADs for the three newly active repositories. A GitHub Search API query for repositories created 2026-11-06 through 2026-11-08 and pushed since 2026-11-06 supplied freshness candidates; Pinky, devvm, and phoneuse were retained after checking their first-party READMEs, while obvious low-quality/noise results were excluded. For the nine Trending entries, gains are the page’s “stars today” values and ordering is descending by those values. The three recent additions are appended, not ranked against daily gains; daily gains are unavailable for them. Totals and commits are live repository metadata and can move after capture.
